# Database Security-Check Matrix

<!-- Generated by tool/ci/pgtap_security_matrix.py --write. Do not edit by hand; CI fails if stale. -->

What kind of security evidence the pgTAP suite (`supabase/tests/`) holds, by product area. pgTAP runs four times in the required database job (incremental upgrade, hosted-ledger backfill, clean slate, post-ingestion), and `tool/ci/check_pgtap_parity.py` requires identical totals each time.

Columns are **static text signals**, not proof. Read a test before relying on its row.
- **Roles**: database roles the tests switch to (`set [local] role …`).
- **Identity switches**: times a test sets the JWT subject; two or more usually means a cross-user check.
- **Denial checks**: `throws_ok`, `throws_like`, `ok(not …)` and `is_empty`, i.e. asserting something is refused or absent.
- **Privilege checks**: `has_table/column/schema/function_privilege` assertions on grants.
- **RLS checks**: assertions that row-level security is enabled (`relrowsecurity`).
- A file has a **security signal** if it has any denial, privilege or RLS check, or at least two identity switches (cross-user tests often assert that another learner's rows count as zero).

**Totals:** 71 test files, 1685 planned assertions, plus 4 files using `no_plan()` (counted only when run; pg_prove reports the full total in the database job).

## Files with no security signal

No denial, privilege or RLS check and fewer than two identity switches. These may be integrity, performance or contract tests rather than security tests. Review whether their area needs a negative-path check.

- `clep_psychology_simulation_test.sql` (Assessment, grading & simulation, 14 assertions)
- `content_primitives_v2.sql` (Content, lessons & import, 16 assertions)
- `content_provenance.sql` (Content, lessons & import, 12 assertions)
